The wing nut is a thick collar carrying three stout radial lugs spaced evenly around it, the lugs squared-off and slightly rounded at their tips — these are what a sledgehammer strikes. The nut turns on a coarse thread cut on the male sub and pulls a shoulder on the female sub against the seat. The union is heavily proportioned for high pressure: a very thick wall section, a deep wing nut and short, stout lugs. Both subs end in a plain unthreaded cylindrical pipe stub with a square-cut, bevelled end prepared for butt welding — no thread anywhere on the outer ends. A dark elastomer lip seal sits in a rectangular groove machined into the male sub's seating face, its section visibly wider and squarer than an O-ring, backing a steel-to-steel seat behind it.
